comment: The bodies of the thirteen homes (docs/bodies-plan.md): a carving brief for each face, the face parameters the body kit reads for the masculine and feminine body (multipliers on the base carving: brow ridge, nose length and width, lips, ears, jaw width, head length, cheekbones), and the skin palette offered at creation (tone ids from data/creation.json, look.skinTones). Every sentence is the owner's to rewrite. dress: the home's outfit as pieces the body kit builds as shells on the body's own rings (tunic, coat, robe, kilt, cuirass, apron, hakama, greaves, boots, belt, sash, collar) in named colours, and a headgear piece hung from the head (cap, hat, turban, furhat), which the look's headgear toggle shows or hides. culture: a line on the outfit, the owner's to rewrite. pieces may carry trim (a band colour at hem, cuff or collar), cuffs, stripes (alternate bands), wide, count; types: tunic, vest, coat, robe, kaftan, kilt, wrapskirt, cuirass, apron, hakama, greaves, boots, sandals, belt, sash, obi, collar, scarf, wrap, gloves, buttons, badge, sashknot, toolloop, pauldrons, pteruges. headgear: cap (peak, goggles), hat (trim band), turban (trim, jewel), furhat, scholarcap, hood, headband, helm (crest), with goggles on any. form is the human each home's people are built from (tools/blender/human.py, MakeHuman's CC0 base and targets): ancestry is the mix of MakeHuman's three ancestry forms (they sum to one), details are MakeHuman's detail targets by short name with a value from -1 to 1 (nose-hump 0.4 is nose-hump-incr at 0.4; a negative value is the opposite target; a name without l- or r- is both sides; head-oval and its like take 0 to 1), m and f add to or override the details for one sex. The brief is the sentence the details were written from. dress.trapping: what the home puts on a genius raised there (game/assets/genius/trappings/<home>.glb, tools/blender/genius_trappings.py), by name and in a sentence. dress (docs/bodies-plan.md, Dress as culture; cut by tools/blender/wardrobe.py): culture, silhouette, chord and signature say it in words; colors names each colour by a ramp of data/style.json and a step (indigo:1.25); stuff says what each is made of (the grain follows); under is what is painted on the body beneath (shirt, legs, shoes: a colour's name, or bare; m and f may differ); pieces is what is worn, each for both sexes or one (sex) and always or in some of the three ways of wearing (in: plain, formal, master: an Instructor's); headgear likewise, one or a list; options are what the creator's Dress page offers (id, name, text, wear, and colors to dye over the home's own). cutOnBody: a piece of one cut that does not fit the other body ({ m: why } or { f: why }): it is not built on that body and the creator does not offer it there, until it fits (npm run check:fit).

alexandria.name: Alexandria
alexandria.brief: Everyone passes through: a face from anywhere, even-featured, a little tired.

dress.culture: The Academy's grey, the same on everyone who passes through: a high-collared tunic under a tabard bordered in brass thread, the cohort's brass tag at the breast, boots for the line. An Instructor wears it long, with the shoulder cape and the chain.

dress.signature: the cohort's brass tag; the Instructor's chain of office

pieces.cutUntilFits: Over the tabard at the waist: in a run the tabard's skirt rides over it (a tenth of the belt sunk, 0.07 deep).

columbia.name: Columbia
columbia.brief: The marshals' city: a long jaw, a straight nose, brows that have heard a verdict.

dress.culture: The marshals' city: a long dark-blue coat open over the gun belt, cream at collar, cuff and facing, brass buttons in two rows and a star at the breast, a red neckerchief, tall boots, and the broad hat. The women ride in a short jacket and a long split skirt. A Captain adds the epaulettes, the red sash and the cavalry cape.

dress.signature: the marshal's star and the gun slung low on the thigh

cahokia.name: Cahokia
cahokia.brief: The river: broad cheekbones, a wide calm mouth, eyes used to reading a current.

dress.culture: The river: a pilot's green oilcloth coat to the knee under a rain cape, a woven sash in ochre and red knotted and left long, boots to the thigh against the water, a coiled sounding line at the hip, and a knit cap. The women wear the woven shawl over a short coat and skirt. A Pilot of the school adds the long cape and the woven baldric.

dress.chord: river green, woven ochre and red, copper
dress.signature: the sounding line coiled at the hip; the sash left long to be seen from the far bank

lunden.name: Lunden
lunden.brief: Fog and docks: a narrow pale face, a sharp nose, ears that stick out under a cap.

dress.culture: Fog and docks and the airship rigging: a short charcoal jacket with a fleece collar under a rigger's harness, a red scarf thrown long down the back, flared breeches bound at the calf, gauntlets, and a flat cap with goggles pushed up. The women fly in a long belted coat and a leather cap. A Dockmaster adds the greatcoat's cape and the steel chain.

dress.signature: goggles pushed up, and the rigger's harness

colonia.name: Colonia
colonia.brief: The engine-works: a square jaw, a heavy brow, a short nose; soot in the creases.

dress.culture: The engine-works: a rust shirt with the sleeves rolled, a heavy black leather apron, gauntlets to the elbow, one shoulder guarded, a tool roll slung across the back and a hammer at the belt, a leather cap with goggles. The women wear the smock, a short apron and the tool bag, the hair tied in a red kerchief. A Foreman wears the waistcoat with brass buttons, the long shop coat and the chain.

tiber.name: Tiber
tiber.brief: The old walls: a Roman nose, a firm mouth, a round head held still.

dress.culture: The old walls: a legionary's red tunic under a bronze cuirass with layered shoulders, studded straps at the waist, greaves, sandals, the red cloak pinned at the shoulder, and a crested helm. The women wear the tunic long under a leather breast-band and one bronze shoulder. A Centurion wears the crest across, the medals on the harness and the armlets.

khemet.brief: The black fields: a long head, full lips, wide-set eyes, a high forehead.

A Keeper adds the pleated shoulder cape and the green mantle.

baghdad.name: Baghdad
baghdad.brief: The house of figures: a fine straight nose, arched brows, a narrow chin.

The women wear the knee-length coat over the same wide trousers, and a veil down the back under a gold band. A Master wears the figured square on the breast, the dark mantle and the chain.

varanasi.name: Varanasi
varanasi.brief: The steps: a lean face, deep-set eyes, a mouth that has sat through the night.

dress.culture: The steps: saffron cloth and little else. The men go bare-chested in a cloth wrapped to the shin with its pleats falling before, another thrown across one shoulder, prayer beads at the neck and the arm, barefoot. The women wear it to the ankle with the end drawn across the breast and down the back. An Elder adds the white shawl, a second string of beads and the veil.

jiangnan.name: Jiangnan
jiangnan.brief: The examination halls: a smooth oval face, a small nose, a composed mouth.

The women wear a white crossed jacket and a plum skirt tied high under the arms with long jade ribbons. Those who have passed wear the figured square on breast and back and the cap with two wings; an Examiner adds the cloud collar.

kazan.name: Kazan
kazan.brief: The steppe: broad flat cheekbones, a wide short nose, a strong jaw, weathered.

dress.culture: The steppe: a gold-ochre riding coat crossed at the breast and flaring from a red sash to the knee, dark fur at its collar, cuffs and hem, tall boots with felt tops, a quiver across the back, and a fur hat with a pointed red crown. The women wear it to the calf under a red sleeveless jacket, the hat with its flaps down. A Khan's Rider adds the string of brass coins and the red cloak edged in fur.

edo.name: Edo
edo.brief: The sword schools: a narrow still face, a small mouth, eyes that do not move first.

dress.culture: The sword schools: a white jacket crossed at the breast, black pleated hakama to the ankle, and the red blade-sash knotted at the hip. The men wear the stiff grey shoulders that stand out past the arms; the women tie their sleeves back with a red cord crossed behind and the sash in a great bow at the back. No hat, the hair tied; a Master wears the black over-coat and the broad straw hat of the road.

builds.comment: The builds every body carries as shape keys beyond lean and heavy (tools/blender/human_kit.py; docs/representation-plan.md). Each is a point on MakeHuman's muscle and weight scales (0 to 1; the fit body is 0.62 and 0.5), with details laid over the home's own (-1 to 1) and an age (0.5 a young adult, 1 the oldest). ownPose: the form is posed and sized on its own joints (age shortens and bows a body; the look's age gives the bow back with the bones). The creator's sliders that blend them are in data/creation.json (look.weights, look.frames, look.ages). Every number is the owner's to change; the bodies are built again after (python tools/blender/body_kit.py all).
